references.text: The children of Israel cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he raised up a deliverer for them—a recurring pattern in the time of the Judges.
The Israelites cried out to the Lord when they were oppressed by Jabin and Sisera, the same cry for help as in the days of Gideon.
The Israelites cried out again to the Lord under the oppression of the Ammonites and Philistines, showing the cyclical pattern of sin and repentance.
The children of Israel cried out to the Lord during their slavery in Egypt, and he heard their cry—the foundational pattern for God's response to his people's distress.
Israel confesses its sin to the Lord after having abandoned him, the same pattern of confession seen in the time of the Judges.
The psalm describes how the Lord again and again heard Israel's cry when they were in distress because of their sins.
The Midianites were declared enemies of Israel who led them into sin and punishment.
The warning that foreign peoples would consume the harvest is fulfilled in the plundering by the Midianites.
